title: Setup: Building on the Parent's Conjugation API
content: The file imports the parent entry cramers-rule-oq-05 to reuse conj U N = U N U⁻¹ and the similarity relation IsSimilar M N := ∃ U, N = conj U M, together with Mathlib's polynomial-algebra library. Everything is stated over an arbitrary commutative ring R and finite decidable index type n. The parent proved only reflexivity of similarity; this entry supplies symmetry, transitivity, and — its main contribution — compatibility with polynomial evaluation.
mathContext: Work over a commutative ring $R$, finite index $n$, matrices in $\mathrm{Mat}_n(R)$ and units $U \in (\mathrm{Mat}_n(R))^\times$. Reuse $\mathrm{conj}_U(N) = UNU^{-1}$ and $M \sim N :\iff \exists U,\ N = UMU^{-1}$ from the parent.
prerequisites: the parent entry's conj and IsSimilar

title: Conjugation by a Unit is an R-Algebra Homomorphism
content: The five laws conj_mul, conj_one, conj_add, conj_zero, and conj_algebraMap show that conj U preserves products, the identity, sums, zero, and scalar matrices. conj_mul is where invertibility is used: expanding (UaU⁻¹)(UbU⁻¹) the inner U⁻¹U collapses to 1 (via Units.inv_mul), leaving U(ab)U⁻¹. conj_algebraMap uses that scalar matrices are central (Algebra.commutes). These bundle into conjAlgHom U : Matrix n n R →ₐ[R] Matrix n n R — a first-class algebra homomorphism, which is exactly what lets polynomial evaluation see through conjugation.
mathContext: $\mathrm{conj}_U(ab) = \mathrm{conj}_U(a)\,\mathrm{conj}_U(b)$ because $U^{-1}U = 1$; $\mathrm{conj}_U(r\cdot 1) = r\cdot 1$ since scalars are central. Hence $\mathrm{conj}_U$ is an $R$-algebra homomorphism $\mathrm{Mat}_n(R) \to \mathrm{Mat}_n(R)$.

title: Cancellation and the Group Law of Conjugation
content: conj_inv_conj shows conjugating by U and then by U⁻¹ returns the original matrix, and conj_conj shows nested conjugations compose along the product of units: V (U N U⁻¹) V⁻¹ = (VU) N (VU)⁻¹, using (V*U)⁻¹ = U⁻¹V⁻¹ (mul_inv_rev). These two facts are precisely the unit arithmetic behind the symmetry and transitivity of similarity.
mathContext: $\mathrm{conj}_{U^{-1}}(\mathrm{conj}_U(N)) = N$ and $\mathrm{conj}_V(\mathrm{conj}_U(N)) = \mathrm{conj}_{VU}(N)$, reflecting that $U \mapsto \mathrm{conj}_U$ is an antihomomorphism-free group action ($(VU)^{-1} = U^{-1}V^{-1}$).
relatedConcepts: inverse of a product of units

title: Similarity is an Equivalence Relation
content: IsSimilar.symm (if N = U M U⁻¹ then M = U⁻¹ N U, witness U⁻¹) and IsSimilar.trans (witness the product V*U) complete the parent's reflexivity. Bundled into isSimilar_equivalence : Equivalence IsSimilar and isSimilarSetoid : Setoid (Matrix n n R), this makes 'matrices up to change of basis' a well-defined quotient — the setting for canonical-form theory and the classification of finitely generated R[X]-modules.
mathContext: $\sim$ is reflexive (parent), symmetric (witness $U^{-1}$), and transitive (witness $VU$), hence an equivalence relation; its classes are the conjugacy classes of $\mathrm{Mat}_n(R)$ under $(\mathrm{Mat}_n(R))^\times$.

title: Similarity is Preserved by Polynomial Evaluation
content: aeval_conj proves p(U M U⁻¹) = U p(M) U⁻¹ in one step: it is Polynomial.aeval_algHom_apply applied to the algebra homomorphism conjAlgHom U (aeval is natural in the algebra). IsSimilar.aeval then reads off that M ~ N implies p(M) ~ p(N) for every polynomial p, with the same conjugating unit. Thus similarity is a congruence for the entire polynomial functional calculus, obtained without any hand-written induction on the polynomial.
mathContext: $p(UMU^{-1}) = U\,p(M)\,U^{-1}$ via naturality of $\mathrm{aeval}$: for an algebra hom $f$, $\mathrm{aeval}(f x)\,p = f(\mathrm{aeval}\,x\,p)$. Hence $M \sim N \Rightarrow p(M) \sim p(N)$ for all $p \in R[X]$.

title: Capstone: Equal Characteristic Polynomials of Polynomial Values
content: Combining IsSimilar.aeval with characteristic-polynomial invariance (re-derived here as IsSimilar.charpoly_eq from Matrix.charpoly_units_conj) gives IsSimilar.charpoly_aeval_eq: for similar M, N and every polynomial p, the matrices p(M) and p(N) have the same characteristic polynomial — hence the same determinant, trace, and (over a field) eigenvalues. Similarity is invariant under the whole functional calculus, not merely under the identity polynomial.
mathContext: $M \sim N \Rightarrow \chi_{p(N)} = \chi_{p(M)}$ for every $p$: apply $\chi$-invariance to the similar pair $p(M) \sim p(N)$. This packages the basis-independence of all polynomial spectral data.

title: Summary
content: The parent showed the classical invariants (det, trace, charpoly) are constant on a similarity class. This entry shows the underlying relation IsSimilar is a genuine equivalence relation and, more strongly, a congruence for the entire polynomial functional calculus: applying any p ∈ R[X] to both members of a similar pair yields another similar pair. The mechanism is that conjugation by a fixed unit is an algebra homomorphism, so aeval commutes with it.
mathContext: Table of results: conjAlgHom, IsSimilar.symm/trans, isSimilar_equivalence/isSimilarSetoid, aeval_conj, IsSimilar.aeval, IsSimilar.charpoly_aeval_eq.
